name: The Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: In the mountains around Snowdon in northwest Wales, huge slate quarries and mines turned farmland into the world's roofing powerhouse. Penrhyn and Dinorwic were once the largest slate quarries on Earth, and you can still see their stepped pits, narrow-gauge railways, workers' villages, ports and grand estates. In 1898, around 17,000 men worked here, and the area's slate and expertise were exported worldwide.
